title: Sunny and the Dingo Pup
description: Little Sonny the quokka has a careful, curious meeting with a young dingo pup. A gentle, brave bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny was walking along the edge of the clearing when he heard a small sound he didn't recognise.

Not quite a bark. Not quite a whimper. Something in between.

He stopped and looked.

There, half-hidden behind a large fallen branch, was a young dingo. A pup, sandy-coloured and small, with enormous paws and ears that seemed too big for its head.

Sunny and the dingo pup looked at each other.

Sunny's heart beat a little faster.

But the pup just sat there, ears forward, tail low. It tilted its head at Sunny in the most curious, uncertain way.

It didn't look dangerous. It looked, Sunny thought, a little bit lost.

Sunny sat down slowly, a safe distance away.

The dingo pup watched him with big amber eyes.

Neither of them moved.

After a long while, the pup lowered itself to its belly in the dust, stretched its front paws forward, and rested its chin on them. Its tail moved once. Twice. A slow, cautious wag.

Sunny let out a breath.

They stayed like that for a while, Sunny and the pup, in the quiet late afternoon. Not friends, exactly. But not afraid. Just two creatures, sharing the same patch of earth for a little while.

Then a sound came from deeper in the bush — a low, soft call — and the pup lifted its head, scrambled to its feet, and bounded away through the scrub, those big paws making soft thumps in the dust.

Sunny watched it go.

He sat for a while longer in the quiet clearing.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, dingo pup. Goodnight, brave and open-hearted afternoon.
